newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgacom says 6,290 staff accept retirement deal.
newsitem.headline: Belgacom says 6,290 staff accept retirement deal.

text.p: Belgian state telephone firm Belgacom said on Friday that 6,290 staff had accepted an early retirement offer which was one of the pillars of the company's massive restructuring programme.
Belgacom said in a statement this meant that about 98 percent of 6,500 workers, from a total workforce of 26,000, who were eligible for the deal had accepted it.
The offer applied to workers from the age of 50 with a minimum of 20 years of service.

The 6,500 had been able until the end of May to accept the deal, which guaranteed them 75 percent of their last monthly gross salary until the age of 60 -- the age at which workers are legally allowed to claim early retirement -- plus a departure premium based on six months pay.

Belgacom said it would now focus on the second part of its deal with trade unions reached in April, the redeployment of about 6,000 employees. The reconversion programme has an estimated cost of 1.5 billion Belgian francs, it said.
Belgacom is 49.9 percent owned by a consortium including Ameritech, Singapore Telecom, TeleDanmark and three Belgian investors.
